title: Signal-fusion traffic smoothing & adaptive admission for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Maya Patel
description: After the Feb 2026 hosted API capacity incident we observed repeated short-lived GPU pool exhaustions triggered by high-concurrency tail traffic and sudden tenant bursts. This ticket scopes a telemetry-driven mitigation that: (1) fuses multiple signals to detect emergent exhaust patterns, (2) smooths upstream request fanout with a light-weight traffic shaping layer, and (3) introduces an adaptive admission controller that enforces fair shares while enabling graceful degrade to lower-cost model variants. Goal: reduce event frequency and mean time to stabilize without user-visible 5xx spikes.
root_cause_summary: The immediate cause was rapid simultaneous prefetched requests combined with a regression in our autoscaler probe window that delayed capacity priming. Amplification occurred because the hosted API front-end fans out retries and prefetches to multiple shards; queue length metrics alone were insufficient to trigger early mitigation. There were gaps in the signal set (no combined burst score), and admission control used a static token-bucket configured conservatively for steady-state not bursty loads.
solution_overview: 1) Build a composite 'exhaust signature' metric combining GPU queue length, slot allocation latency, host-level GPU scheduling stalls, and tenant concurrency slope; emit at 10s cadence. 2) Implement a lightweight traffic smoothing proxy in the request plane that applies a short leaky-bucket per-tenant to limit instantaneous fanout and exponentially back off prefetch windows for suspected bursts. 3) Replace static token-buckets with adaptive admission: token refill tied to pool health signals and a fair-share allocator for tenant priority classes. 4) Add a safety fallback that routes to cheaper quantized model variant when latency SLOs degrade. 5) Provide observability (Grafana panels + alert runbook) and automated remediation playbook hooks for SRE on-call.

progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Incident debrief completed; initial postmortem published. Decided to pursue telemetry-first mitigations rather than immediate capacity overcommit.
2026-02-05: Ethan checked in prototype exhaust-signature aggregator (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-metrics/pull/384). Metric validated against Feb 3 incident trace.

2026-02-18: Traffic-smoother design reviewed by runtime team; concerns raised about added p99 latency in synthetic tests. Decision: keep smoothing window <=250ms and add bypass for low-latency premium tenants.
2026-02-27: Adaptive admission initial implementation landed behind feature-flag (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1122). Canaries scheduled on two non-prod regions.
2026-03-08: Canary observed 42% reduction in amplification events and no user-visible 5xx increase. Found an edge-case where cache warming patterns increased tail latency; mitigation planned (AI-4).
2026-03-10: Preparing rollout checklist and coordinated SRE paging thresholds; security review not required for initial phase.
Notes: remaining work is rollout, additional integration tests, and cost/quality tradeoff analysis.
